title: Renew or restore a tradesperson certificate
summary: You can apply online to renew or restore your tradesperson certificate for various categories of work.
intro:
Tradesperson certificates are issued for 1, 3 or 5-years for the following categories of work:

You can apply to renew your tradesperson certificate online. Your application will be assessed to make sure you meet the eligibility requirements.

You can continue trading while your renewal application is being assessed. If your application is refused, you can no longer trade from the date of the refusal.

To find your certificate number and details, visit Verify NSW.

If your certificate has expired:
who_can_apply: Be a fit and proper person to hold a tradesperson certificate.
Have the necessary knowledge, skills, qualifications, and experience for the relevant trade.
Not be a ‘disqualified person’ under the Home Building Act 1989 or another Act administered by the NSW Minister for Building.
Not be a current apprentice or trainee in the category of work you are applying for.
what_you_need: Your renewal number (as shown on your renewal notice).
Evidence of payment for any infringement notice or fine issued under the Home Building Act 1989 since your last application.
If convicted of any criminal offence in the last 10 years or with pending charges.
If currently on probation or parole, a signed statement from your probation or parole officer.

how_to_steps.text: Select the 'Renew or restore online' button.
Log in, or create your MyServiceNSW Account.
Follow the prompts to renew a tradesperson certificate.

faqs.q: Can I continue working while my renewal application is being assessed?
faqs.a: Yes, you can continue trading while your renewal application is being assessed. However, if your application is refused, you can no longer trade from the date of the refusal.

faqs.q: How do I find my certificate number and details?
faqs.a: Visit Verify NSW to find your certificate number and details.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to renew or restore a tradesperson certificate?
faqs.a: You must be aged 18 or over, a fit and proper person, have the necessary knowledge, skills, qualifications, and experience for the trade, and not be a disqualified person or a current apprentice/trainee in that category.
